# FEAT-012: CLI Polish, Audit, Distribution

> **Status**: [ ] Not started
> **Owner**: cli + release team
> **Depends on**: FEAT-001 (Monorepo Scaffold & CI), FEAT-002 (Yantra Protocol v0 — Zod schemas + JSON Schema emit), FEAT-003 (Chrome Launcher & `yantra doctor` v0), FEAT-004 (Locator Engine), FEAT-005 (Plan Executor — events + checkpoints), FEAT-006 (Security Envelope — sanitizer, AuditLogWriter, SecretStore), FEAT-007 (`ask` Pipeline), FEAT-008 (Recorder Phase 1), FEAT-009 (Annotate UI + Workflow YAML + `lint`), FEAT-010 (Workflow Replay — `run` / `resume` / `RunStore` / `ReportRenderer`), FEAT-011 (Agent Integration — `LLMClient`, provider config)
> **Unblocks**: shipping. This feature is the "everything ships through here" cap on the MVP.

---

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-012
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan.md`

Give Yantra a polished, **POSIX-boring** CLI surface that turns the assembled platform into something a first-time user can install in one command, complete their first task in five minutes, and audit forever after. Concretely, this feature:

1. **Assembles the full command surface** declared in plan §5 — `init`, `config`, `ask`, `record`, `run`, `resume`, `list`, `show`, `workflows examples`, `lint`, `fmt`, `doctor`, `audit`, `report`, `usage`, `clean` — behind a single `yantra` binary, with the documented global flags (`--json`, `--debug`, `--no-llm`, `--config`) and the standardized exit-code map (`0`/`1`/`2`/`3`/`4`). **Init-gating** (plan §5): every command except `init`, `doctor`, `--help`, `--version` requires `~/.config/yantra/config.yaml` to exist; otherwise exit 3 with *"Yantra is not configured yet — run `yantra init` to get started."*
2. **Implements three new user-trust commands** that the rest of the project lacks owners for: `yantra audit <run-id>` renders the run directory into a human-readable audit story; `yantra doctor` (v1) extends FEAT-003's v0 environment probe with LLM-provider, keychain, search-key, and data-dir health checks plus a safe `--fix` mode; `yantra report <run-id>` opens the FEAT-010-rendered `report.md` (via `$EDITOR` or stdout).
3. **Introduces the `ConnectorIO` abstraction** — the internal seam that maps argv → `TaskRequest` and `TaskEvent` → terminal/JSON rendering, in the exact shape future Phase 2 connectors (WhatsApp, email, web) will adopt. Today's only implementation is `CLIConnectorIO`; the seam is what keeps the Phase 2 split from being a rewrite. Per plan §7: "The Connector abstraction lives as an internal interface inside `apps/cli` — argv parsing → `TaskRequest`, `TaskEvent` → terminal rendering — exactly the shape WhatsApp/email connectors will adopt in Phase 2."
4. **Ships the binary** as: an npm package (`yantra` on npmjs.org), a Homebrew tap (`abranjith/yantra`), and a Scoop bucket (`yantra/yantra`), with a single-file bundle produced by esbuild and CI smoke-verified on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
5. **Generates the public documentation**: `docs/protocol-spec.md` from FEAT-002's emit pipeline, `docs/workflow-yaml-reference.md` from the FEAT-002 Workflow Zod schema + `.describe()` annotations, `docs/getting-started.md` (hand-written + verified by an end-to-end "fresh user" CI script), `docs/architecture.md` (high-level package overview), and `docs/cli-json-output.md` (the stable JSON surface for `--json`).

**Why this is one feature, not three or four**:

- The CLI **command surface, global flags, exit codes, and `--json` shape are co-designed** — splitting them would force two features to share a half-baked CLI contract.
- The **distribution channels (npm/Homebrew/Scoop)** are wired to the same release tag and the same bundle artifact; they're a single CI workflow with three publish steps, not three independent features.
- The **audit / doctor / report** commands all consume the per-run directory artifacts written by earlier features; they're the user-facing operator view of the audit trail and belong with the CLI shell that hosts them.

**This feature consumes everything**: every prior FEAT has a wiring file under `apps/cli/src/commands/` that this feature implements. FEAT-010 already stubbed `commands/run.ts` and `commands/resume.ts`; FEAT-007 stubbed `commands/ask.ts`; FEAT-008/009 stubbed `commands/record.ts` and `commands/lint.ts`. This feature **completes those stubs**, owns the global-flags layer above them, and adds the four new commands (`list`, `show`, `doctor`-v1, `audit`, `report`) plus the `ConnectorIO` seam.

**Non-goals (deferred to Phase 2)**:

- Daemon mode (`yantra serve`) — Phase 2.
- WhatsApp / email / web connectors — Phase 2 (this feature only delivers the `ConnectorIO` interface they will implement).
- Token-streaming output to the terminal (FEAT-011 records but does not stream) — deferred per FEAT-011's discoveries list.
- Auto-update (`yantra self-update`) — Phase 2; Homebrew and Scoop handle upgrades natively, npm users do `pnpm update -g yantra` / `npm i -g yantra@latest`.
- Telemetry / crash reporting — never in MVP; local-first per memory.md §General.
- Localized output (i18n) — English only in MVP.
- Bundled Chromium — Phase 2 per plan §3.
- `yantra rerun <run-id>` and `yantra run --start-at <step-id>` — deferred per FEAT-010's discoveries list (tracked in TODO.md).

**Dogfooding north star**: a user lands on the README, runs the install one-liner for their OS, runs `yantra doctor` (green), runs `yantra ask "today's top tech news"` and gets a useful card in under 30 seconds. The onboarding e2e test in TASK-018 *is* this north star, automated.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> Per the plan, Yantra is filesystem-native — there is **no relational database** in MVP. This feature contributes a handful of *build artifacts* (bundled CLI, packaging manifests, generated docs) and a handful of *in-memory entities* (the `ConnectorIO` seam, `CommandSpec`, renderer types, doctor-check types). The future-DB sketch is N/A for this feature.

### 2.1 On-Disk Artifacts

This feature does **not** add new per-run or per-workflow artifacts to `~/.local/share/yantra/`. It owns build outputs and packaging manifests that ship the CLI itself.

| Artifact | Path | Lifecycle | Permissions | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **CLI single-file bundle** | `apps/cli/dist/main.js` | Built by esbuild from `apps/cli/src/main.ts` + transitive deps. Regenerated on every `pnpm --filter @yantra/cli build`. CI verifies size < 5 MB (TASK-014). | Standard repo file perms; on POSIX, the published file is `0755` so it's executable directly. | `apps/cli/build/esbuild.config.js` (this feature) |
| **Bundle source map** | `apps/cli/dist/main.js.map` | Generated alongside the bundle. Published to npm so bug-report stacks resolve to source. | `0644`. | esbuild config |
| **`apps/cli/package.json` `bin` mapping** | `apps/cli/package.json` | Declares `bin: { "yantra": "dist/main.js" }`. npm + pnpm install create the `yantra` shim in the global `bin` dir. | repo file. | this feature |
| **npm publish payload** | files listed in `apps/cli/package.json` `files:` block — `dist/`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` | Built by CI; published on tag push to `v*.*.*`. | `0644` files; `0755` for `dist/main.js`. | TASK-015 |
| **npm postinstall script** | `apps/cli/scripts/postinstall.cjs` | Runs at end of `npm i -g yantra`; prints "Run `yantra doctor` to verify your environment". Honors `npm_config_ignore_scripts` and `CI=1` (silent in CI). Exits 0 always — postinstall failure must never block install. | `0755`. | TASK-015 |
| **Homebrew formula** | `packaging/homebrew/yantra.rb` (committed) — published to `abranjith/homebrew-yantra` tap on tagged release | Auto-bumped by `.github/workflows/release-homebrew.yml`: computes SHA256 of the npm tarball, rewrites `url` + `sha256` + `version` in the formula, commits to the tap repo. | **Generated `docs/protocol-spec.md`** | `docs/protocol-spec.md` | Regenerated by `pnpm docs:protocol` on every CI build; commit-checked drift via `pnpm docs:protocol -- --check` (fails build if dirty). Source of truth: `packages/protocol/src/**.ts` Zod schemas + `.describe()` calls (per memory.md §Documentation). | `0644`. | TASK-017 (this feature drives invocation; FEAT-002 owns the emit code) |

| **`docs/getting-started.md`** | `docs/getting-started.md` | Hand-written; CI runs TASK-018's onboarding e2e script which mechanically executes the commands listed in this doc — if a command in the doc no longer exists or its output shape drifts, the e2e test fails. | `0644`. | TASK-017 |

**Atomic-write convention** (for the doc generators in TASK-017): write `<file>.tmp`, fsync, `fs.rename`. Same pattern as FEAT-009 / FEAT-010. Doc generators are idempotent: running them twice in succession produces a zero-diff result.

### 2.2 In-Memory Entities

All types live under `apps/cli/src/` and are exported from the package-private `apps/cli/src/index.ts` (the CLI is an app, not a library — no public package boundary).

#### 2.2.1 `ConnectorIO` — the future Connector seam (`apps/cli/src/connector-io.ts`)

The **load-bearing abstraction** this feature introduces. Today it has one implementation; in Phase 2 it gains three more (WhatsApp, email, web). Designing it correctly *now* keeps the Phase 2 split a mechanical refactor.

```ts
import type { TaskRequest, TaskEvent, RunOutcome, AskOutcome } from "@yantra/protocol";

/**
 * The seam between an external IO surface and Yantra's inline executor.
 *
 * Responsibilities (and only these — keep the interface narrow):
 *   1. Translate an external input (argv for CLI; webhook payload for WhatsApp; web form
 *      submit for the future webapp) into a typed TaskRequest.
 *   2. Subscribe to the TaskEvent stream produced by the executor and render those events
 *      back to the external surface in a way appropriate for that medium.
 *   3. Render a final outcome (RunOutcome | AskOutcome) and signal completion / exit.
 *
 * Out of scope (kept in the surface-specific layer):
 *   - Lifecycle of the executor itself (orchestrators live in packages/core).
 *   - Persistence of TaskRequest / TaskEvent — those go through RunStore / events.jsonl.
 *   - Authentication / authorization (Phase 2 connector concern).
 */
export interface ConnectorIO {
  /** Identity for logging / audit. e.g., "cli", "whatsapp", "email", "web". */
  readonly id: ConnectorId;

  /**
   * Build a TaskRequest from the connector's native input shape.
   * For CLI: parsed-argv → TaskRequest. For Phase 2 connectors: webhook body → TaskRequest.
   * Implementations must defensively Zod-validate before returning.
   */
  buildTaskRequest(input: unknown): Promise<TaskRequest>;

  /**
   * Subscribe to the event stream for the lifetime of one task.
   * Returns a disposer; the orchestrator calls it on TaskCompleted / TaskFailed.
   * The handler is called once per event in order; implementations must not block.
   */
  onEvent(handler: (event: TaskEvent) => void): () => void;

  /**
   * Render the final outcome to the connector's surface.
   * For CLI: terminal card or JSON to stdout. For WhatsApp: message + media.
   * The renderer is allowed to mutate process state (exit code, stdout) for CLI;
   * Phase 2 connectors return a typed reply object instead — this is the only
   * place the CLI implementation diverges from future connectors, and it's
   * documented as such.
   */
  renderResult(result: ConnectorResult, opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
}

export type ConnectorId = "cli" | "whatsapp" | "email" | "web";

export type ConnectorResult =
  | { readonly kind: "ask";   readonly outcome: AskOutcome }
  | { readonly kind: "run";   readonly outcome: RunOutcome }
  | { readonly kind: "list";  readonly items: readonly unknown[] }
  | { readonly kind: "show";  readonly item: unknown }
  | { readonly kind: "lint";  readonly findings: readonly LintFinding[]; readonly hadErrors: boolean }
  | { readonly kind: "doctor"; readonly result: DoctorResult }
  | { readonly kind: "audit"; readonly report: AuditReport }
  | { readonly kind: "report"; readonly markdown: string };

export interface ConnectorRenderOpts {
  readonly json: boolean;        // --json flag
  readonly debug: boolean;       // --debug flag
  readonly noColor: boolean;     // NO_COLOR env or non-TTY
  readonly stream: NodeJS.WritableStream;  // stdout (or test-injected buffer)
  readonly errStream: NodeJS.WritableStream; // stderr
}

/** Shared lint-finding shape — re-exports from FEAT-009 but lives here so connectors don't need to import core types. */
export interface LintFinding {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly line: number;
  readonly column: number;
  readonly severity: "error" | "warning";
  readonly message: string;
  readonly ruleId: string;
}
```

`CLIConnectorIO` is the single MVP implementation. It accepts the commander-parsed argv as `input`, validates it with a per-command Zod schema, calls into the relevant core orchestrator (`AskPipeline` from FEAT-007, `RunOrchestrator` from FEAT-010, …), subscribes to events via the FEAT-005 `EventBus`, and renders via `TerminalRenderer` / `JSONRenderer`.

**The interface is small on purpose**: three methods, no lifecycle hooks beyond event subscription. The Phase 2 split should not need to change this shape — only add new implementations. Property test in TASK-018 confirms `CLIConnectorIO` satisfies the contract; a `FakeConnectorIO` in `apps/cli/tests/` is the mock used by every command's unit tests.

#### 2.2.2 `CommandSpec` — declarative command metadata (`apps/cli/src/commands/types.ts`)

Each subcommand exports a `CommandSpec` consumed by `main.ts`'s commander registration loop. This avoids spreading commander-API boilerplate across 10 files.

```ts
import type { Command } from "commander";
import type { ConnectorIO } from "../connector-io";

/**
 * Declarative metadata for one subcommand. main.ts iterates these to register
 * commander commands; each spec's `handler` runs after argv parsing.
 */
export interface CommandSpec<TArgs = unknown> {
  /** Subcommand name as the user types it. e.g., "ask", "run", "resume". */
  readonly name: string;

  /** One-line description shown in `yantra --help`. */
  readonly description: string;

  /** Builder that adds args/options to a commander Command instance. Kept declarative — no logic here. */
  readonly configure: (cmd: Command) => Command;

  /**
   * Zod schema validating the parsed-argv shape. Run BEFORE handler. Validation failure
   * exits with code 1 and a formatted error message (TASK-001's error layer).
   */
  readonly argSchema: import("zod").ZodSchema<TArgs>;

  /**
   * Handler. Receives validated args + the global ConnectorIO + global flags.
   * Returns a typed CommandOutcome; main.ts maps it to the exit code.
   * The handler must NEVER call process.exit directly — exit-code mapping is centralized.
   */
  readonly handler: (
    args: TArgs,
    deps: CommandDeps
  ) => Promise<CommandOutcome>;
}

export interface CommandDeps {
  readonly connector: ConnectorIO;
  readonly globals: GlobalFlags;
  readonly logger: import("pino").Logger;
  readonly clock: { now: () => Date };
  readonly env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
  /** Lazy factories — built only if the command needs them. Keeps `yantra --version` from importing puppeteer. */
  readonly factories: CommandFactories;
}

export interface GlobalFlags {
  readonly json: boolean;
  readonly debug: boolean;
  readonly noLlm: boolean;
  readonly configPath: string | null;
  readonly noColor: boolean;
}

export interface CommandFactories {
  readonly askPipeline: () => Promise<import("@yantra/core").AskPipeline>;
  readonly runOrchestrator: () => Promise<import("@yantra/core").RunOrchestrator>;
  readonly recorder: () => Promise<import("@yantra/core").Recorder>;
  readonly annotator: () => Promise<import("@yantra/core").Annotator>;
  readonly workflowStore: () => Promise<import("@yantra/core").WorkflowStore>;
  readonly runStore: () => Promise<import("@yantra/core").RunStore>;
  readonly secretStore: () => Promise<import("@yantra/core").SecretStore>;
  readonly llmClient: () => Promise<import("@yantra/agent").LLMClient>;
  readonly linter: () => Promise<import("@yantra/core").WorkflowLinter>;
}

export type CommandOutcome =
  | { readonly kind: "ok" }
  | { readonly kind: "validation_error"; readonly message: string }   // → exit 1
  | { readonly kind: "execution_failure"; readonly reportPath: string | null; readonly message: string }  // → exit 2
  | { readonly kind: "environment_failure"; readonly message: string; readonly remediation: string }      // → exit 3
  | { readonly kind: "user_handoff_abort"; readonly reason: string };  // → exit 4
```

#### 2.2.3 Renderer types (`apps/cli/src/render/types.ts`)

```ts
/**
 * The pair of renderers that ConnectorRenderOpts.json toggles between.
 * Both are pure functions w.r.t. their input — side effects are limited to writing
 * to the WritableStream passed in opts. No process.exit, no global state.
 */
export interface OutputRenderer {
  renderAsk(outcome: import("@yantra/core").AskOutcome, opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
  renderRun(outcome: import("@yantra/core").RunOutcome, opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
  renderList(items: readonly ListItem[], opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
  renderShow(item: ShowItem, opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
  renderLint(findings: readonly LintFinding[], opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
  renderDoctor(result: DoctorResult, opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
  renderAudit(report: AuditReport, opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
  renderReport(markdown: string, opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): Promise<void>;
  /** Streamed per-event rendering during a long-running command. Spinners, step ticks, etc. */
  renderEvent(event: import("@yantra/protocol").TaskEvent, opts: ConnectorRenderOpts): void;
}

/** Two concrete implementations. */
export class TerminalRenderer implements OutputRenderer { /* boxen + chalk + ora */ }
export class JSONRenderer implements OutputRenderer { /* stable JSON Lines or single-object output */ }

export type ListItem =
  | { readonly kind: "workflow"; readonly name: string; readonly version: number; readonly description: string; readonly modifiedAt: string }
  | { readonly kind: "run"; readonly runId: string; readonly workflowName: string; readonly status: string; readonly startedAt: string; readonly durationMs: number | null };

export type ShowItem =
  | { readonly kind: "workflow"; readonly workflow: import("@yantra/protocol").Workflow; readonly locatorCounts: Record<string, number> }
  | { readonly kind: "run"; readonly run: import("@yantra/core").Run; readonly events: readonly import("@yantra/protocol").TaskEvent[] };
```

#### 2.2.4 `DoctorCheck` and `DoctorResult` — doctor v1 (`apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-types.ts`)

```ts
/**
 * One probe of the user's environment. Each check is independently runnable
 * (no inter-check dependencies — keeps `yantra doctor` parallelizable and
 * keeps a failing check from masking others).
 */
export interface DoctorCheck {
  readonly id: DoctorCheckId;
  readonly title: string;              // shown in terminal output: "Chrome installed and recent"
  readonly category: DoctorCategory;
  /**
   * The probe. Returns a structured result. May read env, config, filesystem,
   * keychain, or do a localhost-only network check (Ollama). Must NEVER make
   * outbound network calls (Anthropic key probe verifies presence, not validity —
   * we never call out without explicit user action).
   */
  run(deps: DoctorDeps): Promise<DoctorCheckResult>;
  /**
   * Optional safe auto-remediation. Only called when --fix is passed AND the
   * check returned a "fixable" status. Side effects must be limited to:
   *   - mkdir -p the expected directories
   *   - chmod 0700 / 0600 on existing yantra dirs/files
   *   - touch missing config file with a commented-out template
   * Forbidden: installing software, modifying keychain entries, network I/O.
   */
  fix?: (deps: DoctorDeps) => Promise<DoctorFixResult>;
}

export type DoctorCategory = "binaries" | "filesystem" | "keychain" | "providers" | "search" | "compatibility";

export type DoctorCheckId =
  // From FEAT-003 v0 (carried forward):
  | "chrome.installed"
  | "chrome.version"
  | "chrome.profile-dir-writable"
  | "runs-dir-writable"
  | "config-readable"
  // New in v1 (this feature):
  | "keychain.accessible"
  | "providers.anthropic.api-key"
  | "providers.ollama.reachable"
  | "providers.config-consistent"
  | "search.tavily.api-key"
  | "search.brave.api-key"
  | "compatibility.pi-agent-core"
  | "filesystem.permissions"            // warns on world-readable ~/.local/share/yantra/
  | "filesystem.orphan-profiles"        // profiles/ with no matching workflow YAML
  | "filesystem.stale-runs"             // runs/ older than retentionDays
  | "filesystem.disk-space";            // warns < 500 MB free in dataDir

export interface DoctorDeps {
  readonly env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
  readonly config: import("@yantra/core").YantraConfig | null;
  readonly paths: import("@yantra/core").YantraPaths;
  readonly secretStore: import("@yantra/core").SecretStore;
  readonly logger: import("pino").Logger;
}

export type DoctorStatus = "ok" | "warn" | "fail";

export interface DoctorCheckResult {
  readonly id: DoctorCheckId;
  readonly status: DoctorStatus;
  readonly summary: string;            // one-line shown in terminal
  readonly detail?: string;            // shown when --debug or --json
  readonly fixable: boolean;           // if true and --fix passed, fix() is invoked
  readonly remediation?: string;       // human-readable next step (shown when status != ok)
  readonly durationMs: number;
}

export interface DoctorFixResult {
  readonly id: DoctorCheckId;
  readonly applied: boolean;
  readonly summary: string;
  readonly newStatus: DoctorStatus;
}

export interface DoctorResult {
  readonly checks: readonly DoctorCheckResult[];
  readonly fixes: readonly DoctorFixResult[];   // empty unless --fix
  readonly overall: "ok" | "warn" | "fail";    // worst status across checks
  readonly version: string;                     // CLI semver
  readonly platform: NodeJS.Platform;
  readonly nodeVersion: string;
}
```

#### 2.2.5 `AuditReport` — the `yantra audit` rendered story (`apps/cli/src/commands/audit-types.ts`)

```ts
/**
 * Structured audit narrative produced by `yantra audit <run-id>`.
 * The TerminalRenderer renders this as prose; the JSONRenderer emits the shape as-is.
 *
 * The audit story is built by reading (READ-ONLY) the run dir's:
 *   - manifest.json    (FEAT-010)
 *   - plan.json        (FEAT-002 schema; FEAT-010 writes)
 *   - agent.jsonl      (FEAT-006 AuditLogWriter; FEAT-011 fills)
 *   - secrets.jsonl    (FEAT-006)
 *   - events.jsonl     (FEAT-005)
 *   - outputs.json     (FEAT-010)
 *   - checkpoints/     (FEAT-005)
 * No writes. No re-execution. Idempotent.
 */
export interface AuditReport {
  readonly runId: string;
  readonly workflowName: string;
  readonly status: "completed" | "failed" | "aborted" | "paused" | "running";
  readonly startedAt: string;
  readonly endedAt: string | null;
  readonly durationMs: number | null;

  /** "The agent saw X." */
  readonly agent: AuditAgentSection;
  /** "The agent requested Y secrets." */
  readonly secrets: AuditSecretsSection;
  /** "The engine did Z." */
  readonly engine: AuditEngineSection;
  /** Outputs surfaced (with retention indicator), plus structured warnings. */
  readonly outputs: AuditOutputsSection;
  /** Cross-cutting summary used by both renderers. */
  readonly summary: AuditSummarySection;
}

export interface AuditAgentSection {
  readonly llmCallCount: number;
  readonly providerIds: readonly string[];        // from agent.jsonl
  readonly modelsUsed: readonly string[];
  readonly totalLatencyMs: number;
  readonly totalCostUsd: number | null;            // null if any call's cost was null
  readonly sanitizationProfiles: readonly string[]; // distinct security_class values seen across the run
  readonly violations: readonly string[];          // any sanitizer-guard violations recorded — should be empty
}

export interface AuditSecretsSection {
  readonly keyLookups: readonly { readonly key: string; readonly stepId: string; readonly ts: string }[];
  readonly distinctKeys: readonly string[];        // sorted, unique
  /** Never present. Documented for the reader: NO VALUES are ever surfaced. */
  readonly values: never;
}

export interface AuditEngineSection {
  readonly steps: readonly {
    readonly stepId: string;
    readonly type: string;                          // protocol step verb
    readonly scope: "public" | "read-only-data" | "authenticated";
    readonly status: "completed" | "failed" | "retried" | "skipped";
    readonly attempts: number;
    readonly durationMs: number;
    readonly candidatesTried?: readonly { kind: string; matched: boolean }[];  // for locator-resolved steps
  }[];
  readonly ethicsRefusals: readonly { readonly host: string; readonly rule: string; readonly reason: string }[];
  readonly checkpointCount: number;
}

export interface AuditOutputsSection {
  readonly persisted: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;   // from outputs.json (retention=persisted only)
  readonly transientNames: readonly string[];              // names of transient outputs (values not exposed in audit)
  readonly outputEvalWarnings: readonly string[];          // from report.md's warnings section
}

export interface AuditSummarySection {
  readonly scopeMix: { readonly publicCount: number; readonly readOnlyDataCount: number; readonly authenticatedCount: number };
  readonly reportPath: string;                             // relative path to report.md
  readonly trustNarrative: string;                         // 2-3 sentences synthesized at render time
}
```

The **trust narrative** is the headline of `yantra audit`: a 2-3 sentence prose summary built from the structured fields above, intended to be readable by a non-engineer. Example:

> "Run completed in 14.3 s. The agent made 2 LLM calls (anthropic, claude-sonnet-4-…), saw sanitized HTML from 1 read-only-data extract, and never received literal secrets. The engine resolved 7 of 7 steps on first attempt, looked up 2 secrets (`bank.username`, `bank.password`) at the moments their fill steps fired, and wrote outputs to `outputs.json`. No ethics refusals."

The narrative is generated by a small templating function (`renderTrustNarrative(report)`) with snapshot tests in TASK-012.

### 2.3 Repository-Style Interfaces

The CLI **does not** introduce new persistence repositories — every persistence boundary it touches is already owned by an earlier feature:

| Surface | Repository | Owned by |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow YAML files | `WorkflowStore` | FEAT-009 |
| Run dirs | `RunStore` | FEAT-010 |
| Secrets | `SecretStore` | FEAT-006 |
| Browser profiles | `ProfileStore` | FEAT-003 |
| Audit-log entries | `AuditLogWriter` (write); CLI just reads files | FEAT-006 |
| Yantra config (`~/.config/yantra/config.yaml`) | `YantraConfigStore` (read-only in MVP) | FEAT-003 |

The new **in-app** interface introduced by this feature is `ConnectorIO` (see §2.2.1). Its single MVP implementation `CLIConnectorIO` is a *strategy* in the connector-strategy sense; FEAT-009's `Annotator` is an example of a similar surface-specific strategy.

A `FakeConnectorIO` lives under `apps/cli/tests/` for unit tests of the command handlers — it captures `buildTaskRequest` inputs, exposes a programmable event stream, and records `renderResult` calls.

### 2.4 Forward-Looking DB Schema Sketch

**Not applicable.** Per memory.md §Project Structure, Yantra MVP persists workflows/runs/profiles/secrets on the filesystem and in the OS keychain. The Phase 2 daemon's SQLite schema is sketched in FEAT-010 §2 — this feature does not contribute any tables. The CLI consumes the filesystem repositories directly.

### 2.5 Relationships

- One `CLIConnectorIO` instance per process. Globally constructed in `main.ts`. Single-task lifecycle.
- One `OutputRenderer` per process: `TerminalRenderer` if stdout is a TTY and `NO_COLOR` is unset and `--json` is unset; otherwise `JSONRenderer`. The renderer choice is captured at process start; commands cannot toggle mid-run.
- Many `DoctorCheck` instances → one `DoctorResult`. Checks run with `Promise.allSettled` (per TASK-011); a single-check failure never throws past the doctor command boundary.
- One `CommandSpec` per subcommand → registered into the single `commander` `program`. The `--version` / `--help` commands are commander-built-in.

### 2.6 Indexes & Constraints (filesystem + interface level)

- **Single-instance constraint on `yantra` invocations operating on the same run dir**: enforced by FEAT-010's `<run-root>/.lock` file. This feature inherits the behavior — `audit`/`report` are read-only and explicitly do not take the lock; `run`/`resume` do.
- **Stable JSON-output contract**: `apps/cli/src/render/json-schemas.ts` exports a Zod schema per `--json` output shape. Schemas carry a `schemaVersion: "0.1"` field; any breaking shape change requires a major-version bump documented in `docs/cli-json-output.md` and CHANGELOG.md (TASK-004). Property test asserts every `JSONRenderer.render*` output validates against its schema.
- **Bundle size budget**: `dist/main.js` ≤ 5 MB enforced in CI. The budget exists to keep `npm i -g yantra` fast and to surface accidental dep bloat (e.g., pulling in `puppeteer` instead of `puppeteer-core`). See TASK-014.
- **Generated-doc drift constraint**: TASK-017's CI step `pnpm docs:check` runs the doc generators with `--check` and fails the build if any generated file differs from its committed copy.

## 3. Files

Source files (all new):

- `apps/cli/src/main.ts` — Entry point. Reads global flags, builds `CommandDeps` (logger, clock, factories, env), registers each `CommandSpec` with commander, runs the parser, awaits the handler, maps `CommandOutcome` → exit code. Imports every `commands/*` module's `spec` export.
- `apps/cli/src/exit-codes.ts` — Single source of truth for exit-code constants. Exports `EXIT.OK = 0`, `EXIT.VALIDATION = 1`, `EXIT.EXECUTION_FAILURE = 2`, `EXIT.ENVIRONMENT_FAILURE = 3`, `EXIT.USER_HANDOFF = 4`. Plus `exitCodeFor(outcome: CommandOutcome): number`.
- `apps/cli/src/global-flags.ts` — Parses + Zod-validates global flags (`--json`, `--debug`, `--no-llm`, `--config <path>`, `--no-color`). Exports `GlobalFlags` type and `parseGlobalFlags(argv: string[]): { globals, residualArgv }`.
- `apps/cli/src/connector-io.ts` — `ConnectorIO` interface (from §2.2.1) + `CLIConnectorIO` implementation: takes a `Command` (commander), wraps the FEAT-005 `EventBus` subscription, delegates rendering to the active `OutputRenderer`.
- `apps/cli/src/render/types.ts` — `OutputRenderer` interface + `ListItem` / `ShowItem` types.
- `apps/cli/src/render/terminal.ts` — `TerminalRenderer` implementation using `chalk` (status colors), `boxen` (cards for `ask` and `run` summaries), `ora` (spinners for long-running step progress), `cli-table3` (`list` output). Non-TTY detection: if `!process.stdout.isTTY || process.env.NO_COLOR`, strips ANSI and skips boxen / ora animations. Streams `TaskEvent`s as one-line ticks.
- `apps/cli/src/render/json.ts` — `JSONRenderer` implementation. Validates every output against its Zod schema before writing. Emits **JSON Lines** during streaming (`TaskEvent` per line) and a **single JSON object** for the final command outcome. The two are distinguishable by line count; `docs/cli-json-output.md` documents the contract.
- `apps/cli/src/render/json-schemas.ts` — Zod schemas for the `--json` output shapes (`AskJsonOutput`, `RunJsonOutput`, `ListWorkflowsJsonOutput`, `ListRunsJsonOutput`, `ShowWorkflowJsonOutput`, `ShowRunJsonOutput`, `LintJsonOutput`, `DoctorJsonOutput`, `AuditJsonOutput`, `ReportJsonOutput`, `TaskEventJsonLine`). Each carries `schemaVersion: "0.1"`.
- `apps/cli/src/render/non-tty.ts` — Tiny helpers: `isTTY(stream)`, `stripAnsi(s)`, `shouldUseColor(opts)`. Centralized so the renderer code doesn't sprinkle env checks.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/types.ts` — `CommandSpec`, `CommandDeps`, `CommandOutcome`, `CommandFactories`, `GlobalFlags` (re-export from `../global-flags`).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/ask.ts` — `yantra ask "<question>"`. Wires FEAT-007's `AskPipeline`. Argv schema: `{ question: string; budget?: number; searchProvider?: "tavily"|"brave"|"browser" }`. Builds `TaskRequest{ type: "ask", intent }`, subscribes to events, renders cards on `task_completed`. Honors global `--no-llm` (forces FEAT-007 rule-based path) and `--search-provider` (overrides config).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/record.ts` — `yantra record <workflow-name>`. Wires FEAT-008 `Recorder` then drops into FEAT-009 `Annotator`. Argv schema: `{ workflowName: string; profile?: string; headless?: boolean }`. On annotator save, writes the workflow YAML via FEAT-009 `WorkflowStore.save`. Forbids `--json` (record is interactive) and `--no-llm` (record never calls LLM anyway — no-op).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/run.ts` — `yantra run <workflow-name>`. Completes the stub from FEAT-010. Argv schema: `{ workflowName: string; params: ParamArg[]; paramsFile?: string; budget?: number }`. Builds `RunRequest`, calls `RunOrchestrator.run`, streams events, maps `RunOutcome` → `CommandOutcome` via `outcomeToCommand(outcome)`.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/resume.ts` — `yantra resume <run-id>`. Completes the stub from FEAT-010. Calls `RunOrchestrator.resume`. Confirms when `requiresUserConsent(failureClass)` returns true (per FEAT-010 TASK-007); refuses with `validation_error` outcome when `--json` is set and consent is required (interactive only).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/list.ts` — `yantra list [workflows|runs]`. Argv schema: `{ target: "workflows" | "runs"; limit?: number; workflow?: string; status?: RunStatus }`. Calls `WorkflowStore.list()` or `RunStore.listRuns()`; passes results to `renderList`. Default target is `runs` (matches `git log` mental model).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/show.ts` — `yantra show <workflow-or-run>`. Auto-detects: ISO-prefixed string → run; otherwise workflow name. `--workflow` / `--run` overrides. For workflows: prints YAML with per-locator candidate counts in a sidebar. For runs: prints manifest summary + last 20 events. JSON mode emits `ShowWorkflowJsonOutput` or `ShowRunJsonOutput`.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` — `yantra lint <file.yaml>`. Wires FEAT-009 `WorkflowLinter`. Argv schema: `{ filePath: string; strict?: boolean }`. Pretty-prints findings as `<file>:<line>:<col>  <severity>  <message>  (<ruleId>)`. Exit 0 if no errors (and no warnings under `--strict`); exit 1 otherwise (validation_error outcome).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts` — `yantra doctor`. Aggregates `DoctorCheck`s, runs them via `Promise.allSettled`, optionally applies `--fix` to fixable checks, renders `DoctorResult`. Exit 0 if overall is `ok` or `warn`; exit 3 if overall is `fail`. v1 — extends FEAT-003's v0 with the new check IDs in §2.2.4.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-checks/index.ts` — Barrel export of all check modules.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-checks/chrome.ts` — Re-exports FEAT-003's existing Chrome checks. Adds `chrome.profile-dir-writable` (mkdir+rmdir probe in `profiles/`).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-checks/keychain.ts` — `keychain.accessible` — writes a probe key (`yantra.doctor.probe = "ok"`), reads it back, deletes it. Captures `keytar` errors and renders actionable remediation (e.g., "macOS: keychain locked, run `security unlock-keychain`").
- `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-checks/providers.ts` — Three checks: (a) Anthropic API key in env or keychain; (b) Ollama reachable at configured `baseUrl` (HEAD `/api/tags` with 1 s timeout — localhost only); (c) config consistency — if `provider: anthropic` then key check must pass; if `provider: ollama` then reachability must pass.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-checks/search.ts` — Tavily / Brave key presence in keychain (`tavily.api_key`, `brave.api_key`). Warning, not failure, when absent — the browser fallback works without keys.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-checks/compatibility.ts` — `pi-agent-core` version pin matches the version range `packages/agent` requires (sanity check that pnpm didn't end up with two copies).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-checks/filesystem.ts` — Four checks: writable runs dir; world-readable warning (memory.md §Security); orphan profiles (profile dir present but workflow YAML missing — fixable: rm -rf the orphan profile **only when user explicitly passes --fix and confirms**); stale runs (older than `config.retention.runsDays` default 30 — never auto-deleted; user is prompted to run `yantra prune`, which is Phase 2).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/audit.ts` — `yantra audit <run-id>`. Reads run dir, builds `AuditReport`, renders. Argv schema: `{ runId: string }`. Read-only — does not take the run-dir lock. Emits `AuditJsonOutput` under `--json`.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/audit-builder.ts` — Pure function `buildAuditReport(runDir: string, fs: AuditFsAdapter): Promise<AuditReport>`. Parses `manifest.json`, `agent.jsonl`, `secrets.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `outputs.json`, computes the structured sections. Includes `renderTrustNarrative(report): string`.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/report.ts` — `yantra report <run-id>`. Reads `runs/<id>/report.md`. Default: prints to stdout. With `--open`: spawns `$EDITOR` (or `notepad` on Windows, `open` on macOS); deliberately conservative — no shell-out beyond `$EDITOR`. Argv schema: `{ runId: string; open?: boolean }`.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/auto-detect.ts` — `detectShowTarget(arg: string): "workflow" | "run"`. Pure regex: matches ISO-prefixed runIds (`^\d{8}T\d{6}Z-`). Used by `show`.
- `apps/cli/src/factories.ts` — Lazy factory implementations for `CommandFactories`. Each factory is wrapped in `once(...)` (memoized). Uses dynamic `import()` so commands that don't need a factory don't pay its load cost.
- `apps/cli/src/logger.ts` — Pino setup. Quiet (level=info, no stdout) by default; level=debug + dual-write to stdout when `--debug`. Reuses FEAT-006's secret-shape redactor config.
- `apps/cli/src/config-loader.ts` — Resolves `~/.config/yantra/config.yaml` (overridable by `--config <path>` or `YANTRA_CONFIG` env). Zod-validated. Delegated to FEAT-003's `YantraConfigStore`; this file is the CLI-side caller.
- `apps/cli/src/help-text.ts` — Custom help banner (chalk-styled ASCII brand mark + tagline). Falls back to plain text under `NO_COLOR`. Sourced from a `.txt` file so it's editable without touching code.
- `apps/cli/src/index.ts` — Package-private barrel export (used by `apps/cli/tests/` only — the CLI does not publish a library API).
- `apps/cli/build/esbuild.config.js` — esbuild bundler config. Single-file output. External: `keytar` (native bindings — can't be bundled, must remain installable as a dep). Platform: `node`, target: `node20`. Minified. Sourcemaps inline-linked. Banner: `#!/usr/bin/env node`.
- `apps/cli/build/bundle-size-check.js` — Post-build size assertion. Fails CI if `dist/main.js` > 5 MB.
- `apps/cli/build/smoke-test.js` — Post-build smoke: spawns `node dist/main.js --version` and `node dist/main.js doctor --json` against a clean tmp `XDG_DATA_HOME` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. Asserts exit 0 and parseable JSON.
- `apps/cli/scripts/postinstall.cjs` — npm postinstall script: prints "Run `yantra doctor` to verify your environment". CJS because npm runs scripts before module systems resolve. Honors `CI=1` and `npm_config_ignore_scripts`.
- `apps/cli/scripts/release-prepare.cjs` — Prepares the publish payload: copies `packaging/npm/README.md` over the monorepo README, regenerates `dist/`, validates `bin` field, asserts no `workspace:` protocol entries leak into the published `package.json`.
- `docs/getting-started.md` — Hand-written quickstart: install, `yantra doctor`, `yantra ask`, `yantra record`, `yantra run`. Each command block is **literal-copyable** — the e2e onboarding test (TASK-018) executes them mechanically.
- `docs/workflow-yaml-reference.md` — Generated from the `Workflow` Zod schema + `.describe()` annotations. Carries a "DO NOT EDIT — generated by `pnpm docs:workflow-ref`" banner.
- `docs/protocol-spec.md` — Same pattern as `workflow-yaml-reference.md` but emits from FEAT-002's full protocol surface (Plan, Step, TaskEvent, ValueRef, LocatorChain).
- `docs/architecture.md` — Hand-written one-pager. Mirrors plan §7's package map with links to each package's `README.md`.
- `docs/cli-json-output.md` — Hand-written prose + generated appendix (JSON schema dump) from `apps/cli/src/render/json-schemas.ts`. Documents the schema-version policy.
- `docs/onboarding-test.md` — Brief doc for contributors describing how the TASK-018 e2e script works and how to update it when commands change.
- `packaging/homebrew/yantra.rb` — Homebrew formula. Source URL is the npm tarball (Homebrew supports `url "https://registry.npmjs.org/yantra/-/yantra-<version>.tgz"`); `depends_on "node@20"`. Caveats section points users at `yantra doctor`.
- `packaging/scoop/yantra.json` — Scoop manifest. Same source npm tarball; depends on Node 24.15.0 (suggested install: `scoop install nodejs-lts`). Post-install hint mirrors the Homebrew caveat.
- `packaging/npm/README.md` — Trimmed README for the published npm package (removes monorepo / contributing sections; keeps install + getting-started excerpt + links).
- `packaging/CHANGELOG-template.md` — Template prepended to `CHANGELOG.md` on each release.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — Tagged-release workflow: build, test, smoke (all OS), publish-npm, dispatch-homebrew, dispatch-scoop, append-changelog. Triggered by `v*.*.*` tag push.
- `.github/workflows/release-homebrew.yml` — Repository-dispatch workflow that updates the Homebrew tap. Owned by this feature; lives in the main repo so the formula can be regenerated from one place.
- `.github/workflows/release-scoop.yml` — Same for Scoop.
- `.github/workflows/onboarding-e2e.yml` — TASK-018's fresh-install onboarding test. Runs on push to `main` and on every tag. Sets up a CI runner with no prior Yantra install; runs the install one-liner; runs `yantra doctor`; runs `yantra ask --no-llm "today"`; records + replays a fixture workflow. Tagged `@no-llm`.

Test files (mirrored under `apps/cli/tests/`):

- `apps/cli/tests/main.spec.ts` — Argv parsing → command dispatch table tests. Asserts unknown command exits 1; asserts `--version` exits 0; asserts no command performs heavy imports (uses `--require` stub to record which modules load on `--version` — guards against accidental eager imports).
- `apps/cli/tests/exit-codes.spec.ts` — Every `CommandOutcome` shape maps to the documented exit code.
- `apps/cli/tests/global-flags.spec.ts` — Each flag parsed; `--no-color` honored; `NO_COLOR` env honored; `--config <path>` overrides default; bad `--config` path returns validation outcome with actionable message.
- `apps/cli/tests/connector-io.spec.ts` — `CLIConnectorIO` satisfies the `ConnectorIO` contract (property test: every method returns the documented shape; event subscription is idempotent; `renderResult` honors the json flag). Mock event bus.
- `apps/cli/tests/render/terminal.spec.ts` — Snapshot tests for each render method (with stable clock + stable runId). Non-TTY: assert no ANSI in output. `NO_COLOR`: assert no ANSI. Boxen disabled under `NO_COLOR`.
- `apps/cli/tests/render/json.spec.ts` — Every rendered output validates against its schema. Schema version present and equals `"0.1"`. Property test: `JSONRenderer.render*` never includes any string from a synthesized `SecretRef.key` lookup table as a literal (no-leak property).
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/ask.spec.ts` — Argv → TaskRequest mapping (table test: `yantra ask "x"`, `yantra ask "x" --no-llm`, `yantra ask "x" --search-provider tavily`). Stubbed `AskPipeline` returns canned outcomes; assert renderer invoked correctly.
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/record.spec.ts` — Argv → recorder invocation. Refuses `--json`. Refuses simultaneous `--profile X` and `--no-profile` (mutually exclusive flag test).
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/run.spec.ts` — Picks up FEAT-010's stub-test (now full): argv → `RunRequest`; each outcome → exit code (table test); `--params key=value` and `--params-file` precedence.
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/resume.spec.ts` — Argv → resume call; consent gate respected; `--json` + consent-required → validation error outcome.
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/list.spec.ts` — Default target `runs`; explicit `workflows`; `--limit`; JSON shape.
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/show.spec.ts` — Workflow path vs run path resolution; `detectShowTarget` table test; sidebar locator counts.
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/lint.spec.ts` — Findings formatted with file:line:col; exit 1 on errors; `--strict` promotes warnings.
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/doctor.spec.ts` — Each check id has a test producing each status (ok/warn/fail). `--fix` applies safe remediations only. Failing check does not abort doctor (Promise.allSettled).
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/doctor-checks/keychain.spec.ts` — Probe write/read/delete using a `FakeKeychain` (FEAT-006). Locked-keychain failure path renders the right remediation.
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/doctor-checks/providers.spec.ts` — Anthropic key in env vs keychain vs absent (warn vs fail per config); Ollama reachable vs unreachable (mock fetch).
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/audit.spec.ts` — Builds `AuditReport` from a fixture run dir (success run; failure run; resumed run). Snapshot tests for the rendered prose. No-leak property: synthesize secrets in `secrets.jsonl` keys; assert rendered audit never contains a string matching a credential shape.
- `apps/cli/tests/commands/report.spec.ts` — Reads `report.md` and prints; `--open` calls a stub launcher with the expected path; missing run returns validation error.
- `apps/cli/tests/build/bundle-size.spec.ts` — Asserts the built `dist/main.js` ≤ 5 MB. Skipped when `dist/main.js` is absent (only runs after build).
- `apps/cli/tests/build/smoke.spec.ts` — Spawns `node dist/main.js --version` and asserts output.
- `apps/cli/tests/property/connector-io.property.spec.ts` — Property test: any sequence of `TaskEvent`s passed to `onEvent` is rendered in order and exactly once; no event lost.
- `e2e/onboarding/fresh-install.spec.ts` — Tagged `@no-llm`. Sets up tmp dirs for `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. Installs the bundled CLI (from `dist/`) via `npm i -g <local-tarball>` into a tmp prefix. Runs `yantra doctor --json`, `yantra ask --no-llm "today's date"`, `yantra run fixtures/onboarding.workflow.yaml` (a hand-authored fixture workflow that hits a local HTTP server). Asserts each step exit-codes 0 and produces the expected output shape.
- `e2e/onboarding/fixtures/onboarding.workflow.yaml` — The fixture workflow used by the e2e. Minimal: 3 steps, no LLM, no secrets, no auth. Hits a `127.0.0.1` page served by the test's `http.createServer`.
- `e2e/cli-cross-os/smoke.spec.ts` — Cross-OS smoke (Playwright? no — just `child_process.spawn`). Runs `yantra --version` and `yantra doctor --json` on macOS / Ubuntu / Windows runners. Asserts no-crash + JSON parseable. Doctor allowed to be `warn` (missing provider keys is expected); not allowed to be `fail`.

Configuration touches:

- `apps/cli/package.json` — Adds `bin: { yantra: dist/main.js }`. Lists `dist/`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `scripts/postinstall.cjs` in `files:`. Declares `scripts: { build, build:smoke, prepack, postinstall }`. Adds `dependencies: { commander, chalk, boxen, ora, cli-table3, yaml }` and consumes the workspace packages `@yantra/core`, `@yantra/agent`, `@yantra/protocol`. `keytar` listed as `optionalDependencies` per FEAT-006.
- `apps/cli/tsconfig.json` — Inherits root strict; ESM only; `target: ES2022`.
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — No change (apps/* already covered by FEAT-001).
- `turbo.json` — Adds the `build:cli` / `docs:check` task definitions with the right `dependsOn` chain.
- `package.json` (root) — Adds top-level scripts: `docs:protocol`, `docs:workflow-ref`, `docs:check`, `release:prepare`.
- `.gitignore` — `apps/cli/dist/` and `apps/cli/tests/__tmp__/`.
- `.npmignore` (apps/cli) — empty by design: `files:` in `package.json` is the allowlist (defense-in-depth against accidentally shipping `tests/` or source maps for private code).

## 4. Dependencies

**Internal (other Yantra features):**

- **FEAT-001 (Monorepo Scaffold & CI)** — required. Provides `apps/cli`, the CI matrix, Vitest, Turborepo's `dependsOn` for `build:cli`. The release workflow (TASK-014/015/016) extends FEAT-001's CI.
- **FEAT-002 (Yantra Protocol v0)** — required. The CLI consumes `TaskRequest`, `Workflow`, `Plan`, `Step`, `TaskEvent` from the protocol package. TASK-017's doc-generation pipeline calls FEAT-002's `emitJsonSchema` and `.describe()` extractor.
- **FEAT-003 (Chrome Launcher & `yantra doctor` v0)** — required. v1 doctor (TASK-011) **extends** v0; v0 checks (chrome.installed, chrome.version, chrome.profile-dir-writable, runs-dir-writable, config-readable) are imported wholesale. New v1 checks are net-new. FEAT-003's `YantraPaths` and `YantraConfigStore` are consumed by the CLI everywhere it touches the filesystem.
- **FEAT-004 (Locator Engine)** — required (transitively via FEAT-005). The CLI does not call the locator engine directly; it surfaces locator-resolution events through the renderer.
- **FEAT-005 (Plan Executor & Step Verbs)** — required. CLI subscribes to the `EventBus` for `TaskEvent` streaming.
- **FEAT-006 (Security Envelope)** — required. `SecretStore` consumed by `doctor` (keychain.accessible probe), `AuditLogWriter`-produced `agent.jsonl` and `secrets.jsonl` consumed by `audit`. Sanitizer is **not** directly invoked from `apps/cli` — all LLM paths flow through FEAT-011's `LLMClient` which already wraps the sanitizer.
- **FEAT-007 (`ask` Pipeline)** — required. `commands/ask.ts` wires `AskPipeline`.
- **FEAT-008 (Recorder Phase 1)** — required. `commands/record.ts` invokes the `Recorder`.
- **FEAT-009 (Annotate UI + Workflow YAML)** — required. `commands/record.ts` chains into `Annotator`; `commands/lint.ts` invokes `WorkflowLinter`; `WorkflowStore` is consumed by `list`/`show`/`run`.
- **FEAT-010 (Workflow Replay)** — required. `commands/run.ts` and `commands/resume.ts` complete the stubs from FEAT-010 TASK-007. `RunStore` consumed by `list`/`show`/`audit`/`report`. `ReportRenderer` is **not** called from `audit` (audit builds its own structured report from raw run-dir files); it **is** called from `report` (which simply prints the pre-rendered `report.md`).
- **FEAT-011 (Agent Integration)** — required. `LLMClient` consumed by `commands/ask.ts` (FEAT-007 already routes through it); `commands/doctor.ts`'s `providers.*` checks consume FEAT-011's `ProviderConfig` and `LLMClientFactory`.

**External (npm):**

- `commander` (^12) — argv parser. Per memory.md §Tech Stack.
- `chalk` (^5) — terminal coloring. ESM-native; matches memory.md ESM-only constraint.
- `boxen` (^7) — boxed terminal cards for `ask` and `run` summaries.
- `ora` (^8) — spinner for long-running steps. Disabled under non-TTY automatically.
- `cli-table3` (^0.6) — table rendering for `list`.
- `yaml` (workspace via FEAT-009) — for `--params-file` and config parsing.
- `zod` (workspace via FEAT-002) — argv schema validation.
- `pino` (workspace via memory.md) — logging.
- `prompts` or `inquirer` (workspace via FEAT-009) — `--fix` confirm + resume-consent prompts. **Reuse** FEAT-009's choice; do not introduce a second prompt library.
- `keytar` (workspace via FEAT-006, optional) — keychain probe in doctor.
- `esbuild` (dev, ^0.24) — bundler. Pinned major; not minor — esbuild's API is stable.
- `pkg-up` or `find-package-json` (dev, optional) — locate the CLI's own `package.json` for `--version`.
- `signal-exit` (^4) — ensures cleanup runs on Ctrl-C (close browser sessions, release lock files). Replaces a hand-rolled `SIGINT` handler.

**Notes:**

- **No direct `pi-agent-core` import** — per memory.md §Architecture, only `packages/agent` may import it. The CLI consumes the `LLMClient` interface.
- **No new prompts library** — `prompts` is already in the workspace per FEAT-009. Verify with TASK-001's smoke build that no duplicate prompt lib slipped into the bundle.
- **No `update-notifier` / `boxen-update`** — no telemetry, no phone-home, no "new version available" toast in MVP. Users opt in to upgrades via their package manager.
- **No `node-fetch`** — Node 24.15.0 has global `fetch`. The Ollama doctor check uses it.
- **No Ink** — per plan §3 the CLI uses `commander` + `chalk` + `boxen` + `ora` + `cli-table3` + `prompts`. Ink (React-for-CLI) was considered and deferred — `--json` is universal across every verb (Ink's React tree doesn't share render path with structured JSON); audit-trail-first means terminal output is non-canonical commentary; Windows-day-1 mandate favors well-trodden ANSI libs; cold-start for `yantra ask` matters; the annotate wizard (FEAT-009) is sequential single-task — `prompts`'s sweet spot. Revisit only if dogfooding the annotate flow surfaces a usability wall; the swap is bounded to `packages/core/src/workflow/annotate/prompts.ts`.
- **Bundle externals**: `keytar` only (native binding). Everything else is bundled. This keeps `npm i -g yantra` to a single-file install (plus `keytar`).

---

## 5. Implementation Tasks

> Vertical slices. Tasks are ordered so an implementer can have a runnable `yantra --version` after TASK-001, a runnable `yantra ask` after TASK-005, and a publishable npm package after TASK-014. Later tasks layer in audit, packaging, docs, and the onboarding e2e gate.

### TASK-001: Commander setup, global flags, exit codes, command-spec loop

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Create `apps/cli/src/exit-codes.ts` — `EXIT` constants + `exitCodeFor(outcome)`.
  - Create `apps/cli/src/global-flags.ts` — parses `--json`, `--debug`, `--no-llm`, `--config`, `--no-color`. Honors `NO_COLOR` env. Returns `{ globals, residualArgv }`. Zod-validated.
  - Create `apps/cli/src/commands/types.ts` — `CommandSpec`, `CommandDeps`, `CommandOutcome`, `CommandFactories`.
  - Create `apps/cli/src/factories.ts` — Lazy `once(...)` factories for every dep in `CommandFactories`. Dynamic `import()` inside each factory body so unused deps don't load.
  - Create `apps/cli/src/main.ts` — Build the commander `program`. Register `--version` from `package.json`. Iterate registered `CommandSpec[]` and `program.command(spec.name).description(spec.description)` + spec.configure(cmd). Each command's action: validate args via `spec.argSchema.parseAsync`, invoke `spec.handler(args, deps)`, catch all errors → typed `CommandOutcome.validation_error` or `execution_failure`, call `process.exit(exitCodeFor(outcome))`.
  - The Command registry initially holds a single placeholder spec (`yantra --version` works; subcommand stubs land in later tasks).
  - Add `signal-exit` registration in `main.ts` to flush logs + release any held resources on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`apps/cli/tests/main.spec.ts`, `exit-codes.spec.ts`, `global-flags.spec.ts`):
  - `yantra --version` exits 0 with the version string.
  - `yantra unknownsubcmd` exits 1 with an actionable message ("did you mean: …" via commander).
  - Each global flag parses correctly; `--no-color` honored; `NO_COLOR=1` env honored.
  - Bad `--config /nonexistent/path` → validation_error outcome → exit 1.
  - `CommandOutcome` table → exit code table.
  - **Eager-import guard**: `yantra --version` must not load `puppeteer-core`, `keytar`, or `@yantra/core`. Vitest test using `--require` to record loaded module IDs.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: README "Global flags" section. JSDoc on `EXIT`, `exitCodeFor`, `parseGlobalFlags`. Add a brief "exit codes" appendix to `docs/getting-started.md` (stub at this task; filled in TASK-017).
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/cli build && node apps/cli/dist/main.js --version` prints the version on all 3 OSes.
- **Depends on**: FEAT-001 (workspace + Vitest), FEAT-003 (`YantraPaths`, `YantraConfigStore` for `--config` resolution).

### TASK-001a: `yantra init` — first-run interactive setup + init-gating

> Plan §5 / Important#4 — without this, first-time users hit "no LLM configured" and don't know what to do. Implements the init-gating check that every other command runs against.

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Create `apps/cli/src/init-gate.ts` — a tiny module that checks `~/.config/yantra/config.yaml` (via FEAT-003's `YantraPaths.configPath`) and returns `{ initialized: boolean; configPath: string }`. The `main.ts` command-spec loop calls this *before* dispatching to any handler; if `!initialized` and the requested command is not `init`/`doctor`/`--help`/`--version`/`--config <explicit-path>`, exit 3 with: *"Yantra is not configured yet — run `yantra init` to get started."*
  - Create `apps/cli/src/commands/init.ts`. `argSchema: { reset?: boolean; json?: boolean; chrome?: string; provider?: 'anthropic'|'ollama'|'none'; profileMode?: 'isolated'|'dedicated'|'reuse-os' }`. The non-`--json` path is interactive via `prompts`:
    1. **Chrome selection** — call FEAT-003's `discoverInstalledChromes(): Promise<ChromeCandidate[]>` (a new surface FEAT-003 must expose if not present — coordinated via a TODO note here). Render a numbered list; user selects or pastes a path. Validate the path exists and is executable. Save as `config.chrome.path`.
    2. **Profile mode** — three-option select (`prompts` `select`):
       - `isolated` (default, recommended): per-workflow profile dirs under `~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/<workflow-name>/`. No cookie/state bleed.
       - `dedicated`: a single fresh yantra Chrome profile at `~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/_dedicated/`. Shared across workflows for users who want one persistent session.
       - `reuse-os`: point at the user's existing OS Chrome profile. **Strong warning** before this option: *"This will share cookies, localStorage, and extensions between Yantra and your regular Chrome. Sites you're logged into in Chrome will be logged into in Yantra runs. Yantra recording may interact with extensions in unexpected ways. Continue?"*  Confirmation required.
    3. **LLM provider** — three-option select (`anthropic` / `ollama` / `none` / "decide later"). For Anthropic: prompt for API key (typed input; not echoed); store via `SecretStore.set('anthropic.api_key', value)` from FEAT-006. For Ollama: prompt for `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:11434`) and `model` (default `llama3.1:8b`); HEAD-probe reachability and warn (don't fail) if unreachable. For `none`: confirm the user understands `ask` will use rule-based extractive summaries.
    4. **Optional search-API key** — prompt for Tavily/Brave key (skippable). Stored via `SecretStore`.
  - Write `~/.config/yantra/config.yaml` via FEAT-003's `YantraConfigStore.write` (atomic temp-then-rename per memory.md).
  - `--reset`: backup existing config to `config.yaml.bak.<ts>`, then run interactive setup fresh.
  - `--json` non-interactive mode: requires `--chrome`, `--provider`, `--profileMode` flags (no interactive prompts); fails fast if any is missing. Used by CI and scripting.
  - Idempotent: re-running interactively shows current values as defaults; user can change any subset.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`commands/init.spec.ts`):
  - Init-gate: command `ask` with no config → exit 3 with the prescribed message; with `--help` → exit 0; with `doctor` → exit 0 (allowed); `init` → exit 0 (allowed).
  - Init `--json` non-interactive with valid args writes a valid `config.yaml`.
  - `--reset` backs up the existing config.
  - `reuse-os` profile mode requires explicit confirmation; declining returns to the profile-mode prompt.
  - Provider=anthropic seeds keychain via mocked `SecretStore`; secret string never appears in `agent.jsonl` or stdout.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: `docs/getting-started.md` — "First run" section walks through `yantra init`. Screenshot the interactive flow (text-only; ASCII reproduction in the doc).
- **Verify**: On a fresh user account (no `~/.config/yantra/` present), `yantra ask "hi"` exits 3 with the friendly message; `yantra init` walks the user through setup; subsequent `yantra ask "hi"` proceeds normally.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001, FEAT-003 (`YantraPaths`, `YantraConfigStore`, `discoverInstalledChromes`), FEAT-006 (`SecretStore`).

### TASK-001b: `yantra config` — get/set/list/unset config values without YAML editing

- [ ] **Implementation**: `apps/cli/src/commands/config.ts`. `argSchema: { action: 'get'|'set'|'list'|'unset'; key?: string; value?: string }`. `configure`: `.argument("<action>", "get|set|list|unset").argument("[key]").argument("[value]")`.
  - `list` (default if no action): dump the loaded config as YAML (secrets shown as `<redacted>`); `--json` emits the structured object with secret keys collapsed to `{ kind: 'secret', source: 'keychain' }`.
  - `get <key>`: read a dotted path (e.g., `provider`, `chrome.path`, `search.provider`). Print the value (redacted if it's a secret reference).
  - `set <key> <value>`: write to config; for `*.api_key` / `secret.*` keys, route to keychain instead of YAML. Atomic temp-then-rename.
  - `unset <key>`: remove a key from config; for secret keys, delete from keychain.
  - All paths validated against the Zod schema before write; rejection returns `validation_error` outcome.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`commands/config.spec.ts`):
  - `list` shows secrets as `<redacted>`.
  - `set provider ollama` mutates only the `provider` field; other fields preserved.
  - `set anthropic.api_key sk-test-FAKE...` routes to the (mocked) keychain, not to YAML.
  - Invalid dotted path → `validation_error`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: README "Configuration" section — recommend `yantra config` over hand-editing.
- **Verify**: tests green; manual: `yantra config set provider ollama && yantra config get provider` round-trips.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001, FEAT-003 (`YantraConfigStore`), FEAT-006 (`SecretStore`).

### TASK-003: TerminalRenderer — boxen / chalk / ora

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `apps/cli/src/render/types.ts` + `apps/cli/src/render/terminal.ts` + `apps/cli/src/render/non-tty.ts`.
  - `OutputRenderer` interface (§2.2.3).
  - `TerminalRenderer`:
    - `renderAsk`: one boxen card per `AskOutcome.card`; chalk-color the source URLs cyan; underline emojis (well, status markers) only if TTY.
    - `renderRun`: top-level summary line + a per-step bullet list. Status icon column: `✓` green, `✗` red, `⤺` yellow, `…` for paused. Final block: "Resume with: `yantra resume <run-id>`" if status is `failed`/`paused`.
    - `renderList`: cli-table3 with columns `(name | description | modified)` for workflows; `(run-id | workflow | status | duration | started)` for runs. Status column color-coded.
    - `renderShow`: workflow → pretty-print the YAML (using `yaml`'s stringify with comments preserved) plus a sidebar table of `name → candidate-count` for `_locators`. Run → manifest summary + last 20 events.
    - `renderLint`: one finding per line, `file:line:col  SEVERITY  message  (ruleId)`; severity colored.
    - `renderDoctor`: grouped by category; each check `✓/⚠/✗ title — summary`; trailing `--fix` hint when applicable.
    - `renderAudit`: renders `AuditReport.summary.trustNarrative` as a boxen card; sections below as headed prose.
    - `renderReport`: writes the markdown to stdout verbatim. No transformation.
    - `renderEvent`: one-line tick per `TaskEvent`; spinners via ora for the in-progress step (acquired/released on `step_started`/`step_completed`). Under `--debug`, dumps the event JSON.
  - `non-tty.ts`: `shouldUseColor(opts)` returns `false` if `opts.noColor || !opts.stream.isTTY || env.NO_COLOR`. When false: chalk is replaced with identity; boxen is replaced with a unicode-frame-stripped variant; ora is replaced with a no-op spinner.

  - Non-TTY: all snapshots produce ANSI-free output.
  - `NO_COLOR=1`: same.
  - `renderEvent` with 100 events: ora spinner created exactly once per step (mocked ora).
  - Boxen fallback under non-TTY produces equally readable plaintext.

### TASK-004: JSONRenderer — stable JSON output + schemas + JSON Lines streaming

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `apps/cli/src/render/json.ts` + `apps/cli/src/render/json-schemas.ts`.
  - For each output type (`AskJsonOutput`, `RunJsonOutput`, `ListWorkflowsJsonOutput`, `ListRunsJsonOutput`, `ShowWorkflowJsonOutput`, `ShowRunJsonOutput`, `LintJsonOutput`, `DoctorJsonOutput`, `AuditJsonOutput`, `ReportJsonOutput`, `TaskEventJsonLine`), define a Zod schema in `json-schemas.ts`. Every schema carries `schemaVersion: z.literal("0.1")`.
  - `JSONRenderer.renderAsk` etc.: build the output object, `schema.parse(output)`, `stream.write(JSON.stringify(output) + "\n")`.
  - `renderEvent`: emits **one line per event** with `{ kind: "event", ...event }`. The final command output is a **single JSON object** with `{ kind: "outcome", ... }`. JSON Lines convention — easy to pipe through `jq`.
  - All JSON renderer methods are atomic with respect to interleaving: builds the full object, writes a single `stream.write` call. No partial flushes.
  - Re-runs of `yantra ask "x" --json` on the same input produce byte-identical output modulo `ts` fields (deterministic ordering of object keys via explicit construction).
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`render/json.spec.ts`):
  - Every render method emits parseable JSON.
  - Every emitted object validates against its Zod schema.
  - **Schema-version fixed**: `schemaVersion === "0.1"` in every output.
  - Deterministic key ordering (snapshot test on the byte representation).
  - **No-leak property** (mandatory, per memory.md §Security): inject synthetic `SecretRef.key`s with fake-credential-shaped strings as values into a synthesized `AskOutcome`; assert the rendered JSON contains the `{kind:"secret",key:"..."}` shape and **never** the literal value. Use `fast-check` to generate diverse shapes.
  - JSON Lines streaming: 100 events render as exactly 100 lines, each independently parseable.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Write `docs/cli-json-output.md`: prose explaining JSON Lines vs single-object; one example per command; the schema-version policy. The doc's generated appendix is populated by `pnpm docs:json-schemas` which dumps `json-schemas.ts` as JSON Schema. CI checks drift.
- **Verify**: Pipe `yantra ask "x" --json | jq .` works on Linux + macOS. Windows: `yantra ask "x" --json | ConvertFrom-Json` works.
- **Depends on**: TASK-002, TASK-003.

  - `argSchema`: Zod schema validating `question` is non-empty, `budget` is integer > 0 if present, `length ∈ {short, medium, long}` (default `medium`).

    1. Build `TaskRequest{ type: "ask", intent: args.question, budget: args.budget, searchProvider: args.searchProvider, length: args.length, noLlm: deps.globals.noLlm }`.

    3. `askPipeline.run(taskRequest)` returns `AskOutcome`.
    4. `deps.connector.renderResult({ kind: "ask", outcome }, renderOpts)`.
    5. Map outcome → `CommandOutcome.ok` (success) or `CommandOutcome.execution_failure` (any failure class).
  - **`--no-llm` semantics**: forces FEAT-007's rule-based summarizer, no `LLMClient` call. The `--length` flag still applies (short = 2 sentences, medium = 5, long = 10). Verified by TASK-018's e2e.

### TASK-010a: `yantra fmt <file.yaml>` — normalize workflow YAML

> Plan §5 / Optional: reduces hand-edit diff noise. Same source-of-truth as the emitter; this command is a thin wrapper.

- [ ] **Implementation**: `apps/cli/src/commands/fmt.ts`. `argSchema: { filePath: string; check?: boolean }`. `configure`: `.argument("<file.yaml>").option("--check", "exit non-zero if not formatted; do not write")`.
  - Handler:
    1. Parse the YAML via FEAT-009's `parseWorkflow`. On parse failure: exit 1 with the structured `LintFinding`.
    2. Re-emit via FEAT-009's `emitWorkflow` (which already enforces stable key order, schema header, locator dedupe).
    3. `--check`: compare original vs re-emitted byte-for-byte. If equal → exit 0. If different → print a unified diff and exit 1 (so pre-commit hooks can use it).
    4. Without `--check`: atomic temp-then-rename write of the re-emitted YAML.
  - **Idempotent contract**: `fmt` then `fmt` is a no-op (the property test in FEAT-009 round-trip already proves the emitter is canonical).
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`commands/fmt.spec.ts`):
  - Formatted file is unchanged by `fmt`.
  - Hand-mangled file (out-of-order keys, missing schema header) → formatted version matches the canonical emit.
  - `--check` on a clean file exits 0 with no output.
  - `--check` on a dirty file prints a diff and exits 1.
  - Parse error in the input file → exit 1 with the lint finding.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: README "Workflow editing" section mentions `yantra fmt`; suggests wiring it into a pre-commit hook.
- **Verify**: tests green; manual: hand-edit a workflow file to scramble key order; `yantra fmt <file>` restores canonical order; running `fmt` twice produces identical output.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001..004, FEAT-009 (`parseWorkflow` + `emitWorkflow`).

### TASK-011: `yantra doctor` v1 — extends FEAT-003 v0 with provider / keychain / search / filesystem checks; --fix

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts` + `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-types.ts` + `apps/cli/src/commands/doctor-checks/*`.
  - `DoctorCheck` interface (§2.2.4).
  - Import FEAT-003 v0 checks (chrome.installed, chrome.version, chrome.profile-dir-writable, runs-dir-writable, config-readable) into the v1 catalog unchanged.
  - Implement new v1 checks:
    - **`keychain.accessible`**: write/read/delete a probe entry (`service: "yantra"`, `account: "doctor.probe"`). On macOS, surface the keychain-locked message.
    - **`providers.anthropic.api-key`**: present in env (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) or keychain (`yantra:anthropic.api_key`). Status: `ok` if present, `warn` (not `fail`) if absent (provider=anthropic in config flips to `fail`).
    - **`providers.ollama.reachable`**: `fetch(config.ollama.baseUrl + "/api/tags", { method: "HEAD", signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1000) })`. `ok` on 200; `warn` if config says provider != ollama; `fail` if provider=ollama and unreachable.
    - **`providers.config-consistent`**: if `config.provider === "anthropic"`, the API-key check must pass; if `"ollama"`, the reachable check must pass; if `"none"`, all pass trivially.
    - **`search.tavily.api-key`** / **`search.brave.api-key`**: keychain probe; always `warn` (not `fail`) on absence — the browser fallback works.
    - **`compatibility.pi-agent-core`**: read the installed version from `node_modules/.pnpm` (or `require('pi-agent-core/package.json').version`); compare against the range declared in `packages/agent/package.json`. `fail` on mismatch.
    - **`filesystem.permissions`**: `fs.stat(paths.dataDir())`; check mode bits; `warn` if world-readable (memory.md §Security). `--fix` → `chmod 0700`.
    - **`filesystem.orphan-profiles`**: enumerate `profiles/*` and check each has a matching `workflows/<name>.yaml`. Orphans listed as `warn`. `--fix` prompts to delete each.
    - **`filesystem.stale-runs`**: enumerate runs older than `config.retention.runsDays` (default 30). `warn` with count. No auto-fix (pruning is Phase 2's `yantra prune`).
    - **`filesystem.disk-space`**: `statvfs`-equivalent on `dataDir`; `warn` if < 500 MB free.
  - `doctor.ts` runs all checks via `Promise.allSettled` (so a hanging check can't block others). Each check has a per-check 3 s timeout via `AbortController`. Collects `DoctorCheckResult[]`. If `--fix` and any `fixable` check failed: run `fix()` (with prompts where required), append to `fixes[]`, re-run those checks to get `newStatus`.
  - Renders via `connector.renderResult({ kind: "doctor", result }, opts)`. Exit 0 if `overall === "ok"` or `"warn"`; exit 3 if `"fail"`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`commands/doctor.spec.ts`, `commands/doctor-checks/*.spec.ts`):
  - Each check has unit tests producing each status (ok / warn / fail) — mock FS, mock fetch, mock keytar.
  - `Promise.allSettled` semantics: one check throws synchronously → others still produce results.
  - Per-check timeout: a check that never resolves → 3 s timeout → `fail` with timeout message.
  - `--fix` table test: each fixable check, fix applied, status flips to `ok`. Each non-fixable check unchanged.
  - Overall status: `ok` if all ok; `warn` if any warn and no fails; `fail` if any fail.
  - **No outbound network**: vitest mocks `fetch`; assert no fetch call to a non-localhost URL.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: `doctor` section in `docs/getting-started.md`. JSDoc on each check module. A "Doctor check reference" appendix in `docs/architecture.md` listing every check id + remediation.
- **Verify**: `yantra doctor` on a fresh machine produces a sensible report; `--fix` on a misconfigured dir flips it to `ok`. Cross-OS verified by TASK-018's e2e and TASK-014's smoke.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001..004, FEAT-003 (v0 checks + YantraPaths), FEAT-006 (`SecretStore`), FEAT-011 (`ProviderConfig`).

### TASK-012: `yantra audit <run-id>` — renders run dir as a readable audit story

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `apps/cli/src/commands/audit.ts` + `apps/cli/src/commands/audit-builder.ts` + `apps/cli/src/commands/audit-types.ts`.
  - `argSchema`: `{ runId: string }`.
  - `buildAuditReport(runDir, fs)`: pure function that READS only.
    1. `manifest.json` → runId, workflowName, status, timestamps, scopeSummary.
    2. `agent.jsonl` → group by direction (request/response); count distinct providers + models; sum latencies + costs; collect distinct `prompt_sanitized` length distribution (for the prose narrative); record any `outcome === "validation_failed"` etc.
    3. `secrets.jsonl` → list of `{ key, stepId, ts }` lookups; distinct keys sorted.
    4. `events.jsonl` → per-step events; classify status (completed / failed / retried); pull candidate-trace from `step_completed` events; collect ethics refusals.
    5. `outputs.json` → persisted outputs (verbatim) + transient-output names (no values).
    6. `report.md` → grep for warning-section blocks (so audit echoes any output-eval warnings).
    7. Build `AuditReport.summary.trustNarrative` via `renderTrustNarrative(report)`: template-literal that fills the 2-3 sentence narrative from the structured fields.
  - `audit.ts` handler: `buildAuditReport(paths.runDir(runId), fs)` → render via connector. Read-only — never takes the FEAT-010 `.lock`.

  - Three fixture run dirs (success / failure / resumed): snapshot of the `AuditReport`.
  - Snapshot of the rendered prose narrative for each.
  - **No-leak property** (mandatory): synthesize `secrets.jsonl` with keys whose names look like credentials (`fake-sk-abc`); assert the rendered output contains `(fake-sk-abc)` as a key reference but never a credential-shaped value. Then synthesize `agent.jsonl` with a `prompt_sanitized` field containing a deliberate raw-secret-shaped substring; assert the audit handler refuses to render and instead logs an `error` + falls back to a "this run's agent.jsonl appears tampered" report (memory.md §Logging "never log secrets" — defense in depth even when reading prior-recorded data).
  - Missing run dir → validation_error with hint "did you mean: …" (Levenshtein over `runStore.listRuns`).
  - Corrupt JSONL line → skipped with a warning surfaced in the report, not a crash.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Write `docs/audit.md`: example audit output; explanation of each section; the trust-narrative concept. Linked from `docs/architecture.md` §Security.
- **Verify**: Tests green. Manual: run FEAT-010's e2e fixture; `yantra audit <runId>` produces a useful, secret-free report on all 3 OSes.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001..004, FEAT-005 (events.jsonl shape), FEAT-006 (agent.jsonl + secrets.jsonl shapes), FEAT-010 (manifest + outputs + report).

### TASK-013b: `yantra clean` — garbage-collect run dirs and orphaned profile dirs

> Plan §5 / Important#8: prevents the silent disk-leak from 600 run dirs and 20 profile dirs accumulating over six months.

- [ ] **Implementation**: `apps/cli/src/commands/clean.ts`. `argSchema: { runsOlderThan?: string; orphanedProfiles?: boolean; apply?: boolean }`. `configure`: `.option("--runs-older-than <duration>", "e.g. 30d", "30d").option("--orphaned-profiles").option("--apply", "actually delete (default is dry-run)")`.
  - **Default mode is dry-run**; user must pass `--apply` to delete. The output always lists what *would* be / *was* deleted with sizes.
  - Two scopes (can be combined):
    1. **Run-dir cleanup**: parse `--runs-older-than` (`30d`, `2w`, `1y` via a small duration parser). Enumerate run dirs whose `manifest.startedAt` is older than the cutoff. Sum their sizes. Skip runs that are `running` or `paused` (those are live state).
    2. **Orphaned profiles**: enumerate `~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/<name>/`; for each, check if `~/.local/share/yantra/workflows/<name>.yaml` exists. If not, the profile is orphaned.
  - **Safety prompts** (under `--apply`, non-`--json`): show the candidate list + total size, ask `prompts.confirm` "Delete N items totaling X MB? (y/N)" with default no. Refuse to delete if the candidate list is empty.
  - **`--json --apply`**: requires `--yes` (an additional gate) to skip the prompt — scripting use only.
  - All deletions go through atomic `rm -rf` on a sibling temp path (rename-to-temp then unlink the temp) so a Ctrl-C mid-delete leaves consistent state.
  - Emit a final summary: `Removed: N run dirs (X MB), M profile dirs (Y MB)`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`commands/clean.spec.ts`):
  - Dry-run is the default; no FS mutation occurs without `--apply`.
  - Run dirs newer than the cutoff are preserved.
  - Running/paused runs are skipped regardless of age.
  - Orphan-profile detection: a profile without a matching workflow YAML is listed; one with a matching YAML is not.
  - `--apply` without `--yes` under `--json` → validation_error.
  - Confirm-prompt declined → no deletion, exit 0.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: `docs/getting-started.md` adds a "Keeping your run history tidy" subsection.
- **Verify**: tests green; manual: a fixture FS with 5 old + 3 fresh run dirs and 2 orphan profiles — dry run lists 5+2; `--apply --yes` removes them; second run reports nothing to clean.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001..004, FEAT-003 (`YantraPaths`), FEAT-010 (`RunStore.listRuns` for canonical age data).
